sample_size.events_unit: one TOURNAMENT (event code) = one observation, per P022_DECISION_RULE.md §2 / spec extra.unit_of_observation; R1/R2/R3 pooled. 22 of 24 tournament codes present in the current cache produced >=1 fill and enter the edge statistic; the other 2 (AUAOPBKT26, ISHSO26) posted quotes but never filled.
sample_size.trades_unit: distinct (market, fill) events under spec-compliant sizing (per-name/per-tournament/aggregate collateral caps enforced, see capacity below); 172 of 404 posted markets filled. The uncapped default sizing used by the existing harness (quote_size=25 ct/name, ignoring the $5 per-name collateral cap) fills 183/404 markets for 4,289 contracts -- reported for comparison in extra.
sample_size.date_range: 2026-05-18 to 2026-07-25 (69 days, ~2.3 months) -- bounded by Kalshi's ~1-month public trade-history retention plus successive cache pulls; no temporal holdout exists (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §6).

performance.net_edge_units: USD per filled contract (2.04 cents), net of maker fee (0.0, verified quadratic on all 13 series) and modelled adverse selection. PRIMARY estimate: equal-weighted-across-tournament mean of within-tournament contract-weighted P&L (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §3 formula, literally re-implemented -- NOT the harness's native `net_per_contract` output, see stress_tests.methodology_discrepancy), computed with quote sizing capped at the spec's own registered per-name/per-tournament/aggregate collateral limits (capacity_aware sizing), H=12h pre-close anchor, offset +0.02, band [0.03,0.12], strict-through fills, full current data cache (404 markets / 24 tournament codes, 2026-08-02).
performance.clv_note: No CLV substitute is valid for this family -- round-leader markets have no sharp external closing line and the edge is a certified settlement mechanic (a tie splits $1/n), not a price-disagreement signal. Spec fair_value_model.mechanism_class and P022_DECISION_RULE.md §8.5 both state this explicitly; the integrity review verified the underlying settlement clause verbatim against the primary PDF. Reporting a numeric CLV here would misrepresent a metric this strategy family cannot generate; the key is present (schema-required) and honestly null. Realised settlement P&L (captured in net_edge/uncertainty) is the only valid validator per the locked rule.

uncertainty.method: Tournament-clustered bootstrap (5000 draws, seed 12345, resample tournaments with replacement, equal weight per resampled tournament) on the equal-weighted-across-tournament statistic described above (capacity-aware sizing, H=12, offset +0.02, strict-through fills). CI spans zero.
uncertainty.parametric_check: se = sd(x_t)/sqrt(T) = 1.812c/ct (T=22, sd=8.499c/ct); z = edge/se = 1.13 -- below the locked rule's own significance bar (z>=2.0) by a wide margin; the point estimate would not clear PASS even at T=22 if T=22 were a decision point (it is not; T<24 is NO DECISION by rule).

stress_tests.harness_self_check: PASS -- `python3 backtest_fade_fills.py --validate` reproduces every cell of the published Phase-2 table (net c/ct, CI, tournament counts, E[settle|posted/filled], 16/19 positive tournaments, USO26 leave-one-out) on the pinned 364-market universe, byte-for-byte within stated tolerance. The harness's arithmetic is trustworthy; the finding below is about which statistic it reports as headline, not a code bug.
stress_tests.methodology_discrepancy: MATERIAL FINDING. quirks_common.replay()/bootstrap_weighted() report `net_per_contract` as a single POOLED contract-weighted mean across every filled contract in the sample (large-field tournaments implicitly dominate) -- this is NOT the statistic P022_DECISION_RULE.md §3 defines (`edge = mean(x_t)`, the EQUAL-weighted mean of PER-TOURNAMENT contract-weighted means). On the original 19-tournament published universe the two statistics happen to be close (+3.4c pooled vs +3.80c equal-weight, both z>3, same conclusion) which is presumably why this was never caught. On the current 22-tournament (widened) universe they diverge sharply: pooled = +2.57c/ct [+0.08,+4.51] (matches the figure already cited in the locked rule's Amendment 1, independently reproduced here) vs. the CORRECT equal-weighted statistic = +1.45c/ct (uncapped sizing) / +2.04c/ct (capacity-aware sizing), z=0.65 / 1.13 respectively -- NOT distinguishable from zero either way. Re-verified: `scripts/p022_checkpoint.py` (the sanctioned FORWARD-gate reader, source-read only, not invoked) DOES implement the correct equal-weight §3 formula (`edge = statistics.mean(xs)`, `se = sd/sqrt(T)`), so the forward gate itself is not affected -- but the BACKTEST that justified building the pod, and the sigma=3.781c/ct used to derive Amendment 1's T=24/T=40 thresholds, were both computed from the wrong (pooled) statistic.
stress_tests.power_reassessment: MATERIAL FINDING. Re-solving T=((2.0+z_0.90)*sigma/edge)^2 with the CORRECTLY (equal-weight) measured sigma and edge from the current cache: sigma(x_t)=8.50c/ct (vs. the 3.78c/ct assumed in Amendment 1, derived indirectly from a bootstrap CI on the wrong pooled statistic) and edge=2.04c/ct (capacity-aware) gives T~=187 for 90% power / T~=140 for 80% power -- roughly 6-8x Amendment 1's T=24, and at the decision rule's own measured cadence (13.7 tournaments/month, P022_DECISION_RULE.md §5) that is >1 year of continuous quoting, not ~2 months. This does not by itself invalidate the registered T=24/T=40 rule (Amendment 1 stands until Sam revisits it, and no parameter is changed here), but it is evidence the pre-registered thresholds may be underpowered against the true between-tournament variance and is flagged for Sam's attention, consistent with Amendment 1's own precedent that T=0 (now) is the only moment such a re-solve can be made without touching evidence.
stress_tests.leave_one_out: Equal-weighted point estimate (uncapped sizing, H=12/off=0.02) stays POSITIVE under every single-tournament jackknife (range +1.09c to +3.36c across 22 folds) -- sign is robust to any one tournament, but magnitude is highly sensitive to KIN26 alone (dropping it more than doubles the edge, +1.45c -> +3.36c), which is expected: KIN26 (LIV Golf, small field, 11 markets) contains one 25-contract fill that led its round outright and lost the mechanical maximum of -94c/contract, the same worst-case figure the original Phase-2 report and P022_DECISION_RULE.md §7 already flagged (“worst single-name outcome is -94c/contract”) -- this is realised tail risk recurring exactly as documented, not a data artefact.
stress_tests.time_split_regression_check: First-half vs second-half chronological split of the 22 filled tournaments (11/11, split at the sample midpoint 2026-06-ish): first half equal-weight edge = +3.21c/ct (z=1.72), second half = -0.31c/ct (z=-0.07). The effect decays toward zero across the sample window, consistent with the locked rule's own stated prior (§1: 'Regression toward zero is the expected outcome') and with §6's warning that Phase 2 has no temporal holdout. This is evidence for caution, not evidence the mechanism is false -- the underlying settlement-mechanic hypothesis (certified $1/n dead-heat split) does not itself decay; adverse selection or a shrinking behavioural mispricing component plausibly does.
stress_tests.fill_model_sensitivity: Strict-through (pessimistic, primary) vs at-or-through (loose/optimistic) fills, capacity-aware sizing: +2.04c/ct (z=1.13) vs +2.33c/ct (z=1.33) -- a small, expected difference; conclusion (not significant) unchanged either way.
stress_tests.offset_and_window_grid: Equal-weighted stat computed at every published grid point (uncapped sizing, full current cache): H=12/off=0.00 +1.18c (z=0.91); H=12/off=0.02 +1.45c (z=0.65); H=12/off=0.04 +2.70c (z=1.15); H=6/off=0.00 +0.02c (z=0.01); H=6/off=0.02 -0.29c (z=-0.07); H=24/off=0.00 +1.39c (z=1.30); H=24/off=0.02 +1.09c (z=0.48). No grid cell reaches |z|>=2.0 in either direction; sign is positive at 5 of 7 cells (the two H=6 cells, already flagged as marginal in the original Phase-2 work, are the exceptions) but never separates from zero.
stress_tests.capacity_cap_realism: MATERIAL FINDING. The harness's (and the original Phase-2 report's) default quote_size=25 contracts/name is NOT achievable under the spec's own registered risk caps at these prices. Collateral at risk on a sell-YES fade is (1-quote_px) per contract; in the traded band+offset (quote_px roughly 0.05-0.16) that is $0.84-$0.95/contract, so the spec's per-name cap (0.5% of $1,000 = $5.00) binds at ~5-6 contracts/name, not 25 -- the 25-contract MAX_CONTRACTS_PER_NAME bound in the spec is a secondary/non-binding ceiling in this price band, never the actual constraint. See capacity for the re-sized result.

capacity.estimate_basis: Event-driven replay (quotes/fills processed in chronological close-time order; the per-name/per-tournament/aggregate USD collateral caps are enforced live, with aggregate and per-tournament collateral RELEASED back to the pool at each market's own settlement -- these are ~1-day-resolving contracts, so capital recycles quickly) using the spec's own registered caps: per-name $5.00 (0.5% of $1,000 bankroll), per-tournament $50.00 (5%), aggregate $150.00 (15%, P-022's own book only per spec.risk_limits.cap_scope_caveat), max_contracts_per_name=25 (non-binding here, see stress_tests.capacity_cap_realism).
capacity.comparison_to_prior_uncapped_estimate: The locked decision rule (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §7) records 'Phase 2 projects ~$140 P&L on ~$3.8k collateral per month at 25 contracts/name.' That figure used the same uncapped quote_size=25 assumption flagged in stress_tests.capacity_cap_realism, which breaches the pod's own per-name collateral cap by ~4-5x at typical quote prices. Re-run with the caps actually registered in the spec (this validation), capacity is roughly $370/month gross collateral and ~$11/month net P&L at the measured (not statistically significant) edge -- an order of magnitude below the figure previously used to characterise this strategy's size.
capacity.structural_ceiling: At the decision rule's own measured cadence (13.7 qualifying tournaments/month across all 13 series) and a per-tournament cap of $50 (binding well before the $150 aggregate cap, since round-leader events resolve in ~1 day and rarely overlap), the structural ceiling is roughly 13.7 x $50 = $685/month gross collateral -- capacity is bounded by the number of tournaments the schedule offers and the per-tournament cap, not by bankroll. This is a small, non-scalable strategy at a $1,000 bankroll by construction, exactly as P022_DECISION_RULE.md §7 states plainly ('Capacity is small and that is not a reason to loosen anything... If that is judged too small to bother with, the correct action is to not build the pod -- not to raise the caps'); this validation does not recommend raising any cap.

extra.hard_boundary_respected: This validation targets the RETROSPECTIVE backtest ONLY, per the spec's extra.validation_target and extra.boundary_not_to_cross. No live/forward-gate statistic (edge, se, z, T, verdict) was computed, estimated, or reported anywhere in this run. `scripts/p022_checkpoint.py` was read as SOURCE CODE ONLY (to check whether its formula matches P022_DECISION_RULE.md §3 -- it does) and was never invoked, and no live trade log was read for performance.
extra.go_no_go_rationale: P-022's live forward gate is locked at T>=24 settled tournaments (Amendment 1, 2026-07-28); T is currently 0 and P022_DECISION_RULE.md forbids any early look, treats T<24 as NO DECISION, and states plainly that 'silence is not confirmation.' A retrospective backtest -- however it comes out -- cannot satisfy a gate defined on forward, out-of-sample paper trading; go_no_go='go' would misrepresent that the locked rule has been cleared. Independently, the retrospective evidence itself does not support urgency: applying the decision rule's own §3 formula (equal weight per tournament) rather than the backtest harness's native pooled statistic, the point estimate is small (+1.4 to +2.0c/ct depending on sizing assumption), not statistically distinguishable from zero (z=0.65-1.13, CI spans zero), and shows within-sample decay toward zero across chronological halves. The underlying mechanism (a certified $1/n dead-heat settlement split) remains real and was independently re-verified by the integrity review against the primary contract-terms PDF, so this is not a kill of the hypothesis -- it is 'let the forward gate, which will use the correct statistic, actually run and report at T=24 as pre-registered.' Decision: hold. Nothing here authorises live money, raises a cap, or changes a locked parameter (the spec's parameters were not altered to produce this result, per instructions).
extra.blinding_disclosure: Compute-then-compare order, stated plainly. (1) Before running any computation I read (as required to understand the locked gate this artifact must respect): research/specs/strat_p022_fade_v2_2026-08-02.json, research/integrity/strat_p022_fade_v2_integrity_2026-08-02.json, golf_quirks_research/P022_DECISION_RULE.md (the LOCKED gate document), golf_quirks_research/backtest_fade_fills.py, and golf_quirks_research/quirks_common.py (the harness source). P022_DECISION_RULE.md is not a verdict document but it DOES quote, as background/rationale for its own T-threshold math, both the original Phase-2 headline (+3.4c/ct [+1.7,+5.1], 19 tournaments) and, via Amendment 1, the widened pooled estimate (+2.57c/ct [+0.1,+4.5]). I therefore saw these two point estimates before running my own numbers -- this is disclosed honestly as a real, if partial, anchoring risk; I could not have understood the gate (T=24, HARD KILL at z<=-2.0, the single-extension structure) without reading the document that states them. (2) I did NOT open golf_quirks_research/REPORT_Golf_Quirks_Phase2_P022_2026-07.md, golf_quirks_research/REPORT_P022_Widened_2026-07.md, or golf_quirks_research/p022_p023_params.json at any point in this session -- confirmed by the tool-call record, these files were never Read, only seen in an `ls` directory listing. (3) I then ran `backtest_fade_fills.py --validate` first (harness self-check against the published table, PASS) and only afterward computed my own numbers: first the harness's native pooled-statistic re-run on the full current cache (landed at +2.57c/ct [+0.08,+4.51] -- essentially identical to the Amendment-1 figure already seen in step 1, which is expected since it is the same statistic on almost the same data, not independent confirmation of anything new). (4) The material, NOT-previously-seen finding -- that the decision rule's own §3 formula gives a materially different and non-significant result once correctly implemented, that this diverges from what the harness reports as headline, and that the implied required-T under the true (equal-weight) variance is far larger than Amendment 1 assumed -- was derived by me from raw trade/candle data by literally implementing §3's formula in a fresh script; it appears nowhere in any document I read, including P022_DECISION_RULE.md itself. I judge this finding un-anchored. The pooled-statistic reproduction (step 3) is anchored and is reported as a consistency check, not as independent evidence.
extra.artifacts_produced: This validation report only. No production config, service, rule file, spec, or integrity report was modified. golf_quirks_research/ and the rest of the repo were read-only for this run (git status clean there before and after).
extra.reproduction: python3 golf_quirks_research/backtest_fade_fills.py --validate (harness self-check, PASS); all other figures reproduced by ad hoc scripts run via Bash against golf_quirks_research/quirks_common.py's public functions (anchor_at, settlement_value, per_tournament, replay) -- not committed as new harness files per the read-only validator boundary; the exact scripts are recoverable from this session's tool-call transcript if a permanent artifact is wanted.
extra.fee_and_execution_cost_statement: Maker fee = 0.0, independently re-confirmed against src/fixtures/kalshi_series_fees.json (all 13 series 'quadratic') consistent with the integrity report's live /series check. No separate half-spread deduction is applied because the model already prices it structurally: the quote itself sits at anchor_mid + offset (the offset IS the spread/edge cushion being tested), and a fill is only counted on a real public taker print priced STRICTLY THROUGH the quote (the project's pessimistic convention, refusing ties that might belong to a resting order ahead in queue) -- this is a maker resting-order model, so there is no additional taker-side slippage to add on entry. Adverse selection is measured directly (E[settlement|filled] > E[settlement|posted] in every cut examined) rather than assumed.
